text:
Doing the translation in Israel might not be the best way forward. You need the apostille on the documents for sure, but you can do that yourself at the ministry of foreign affairs in Jlem. 
As for the translation: This is more expensive over here than almost everywhere else, and generally speaking, it is more difficult to get foreign translations accepted, so it might be better to have those documents translated by a notary in Sweden. That saves you also from the obligation to add a second apostille (the one that certifies the notary in question is properly registered and has the language qualification needed).
